A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, research questions, experiments and appendix material. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison throughout. The existing appendices A–F in v1 correspond to B–G in v3, following a new Related Work appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM conversation simulations, quantitative measurements of four socio-cognitive effects, and human evaluations of persona hierarchies and LLM judging. Results appear in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation and human-evaluation results, including the main experimental comparisons and supplementary results in Tables 10–15.

M1.justification: Persona selection, status assignment, conversation simulation, control prompts and GPT-5 judging remain unchanged. The prompt appendix is renumbered from A to B without changing the procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PersonaHub role pairs, DailyPersuasion, Do-Not-Answer and DailyDialogue material. The four socio-cognitive tasks, represented domains and evaluated conversation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Model membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments, including the model-size comparisons, Mistral/OLMo post-training comparisons and human evaluation of judging. Newly cited studies in Appendix A are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Both report the same status conditions, conversation budgets, turn-5/10/15 evaluations, model configurations, scoring rules and human-evaluation sample sizes. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The conversation-progression, prompt-control, model-size and post-training analyses are retained unchanged. The human-versus-synthetic starter analysis in Tables 14–15 and qualitative examples in Tables 19–24 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across conversations, use boldface for statistical significance and retain the same annotation-agreement reporting. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation or statistical-testing practice changes are reported.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative experimental findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 4 retains Qwen 2.5 7B persuasion success of 25.0% for low-status initiators and 30.9% for high-status initiators.

T1.justification: Definitions of pronoun effects, coordination degree and status-difference measures remain unchanged. Neither version contains a new or revised theorem, proof or mathematical derivation relative to the other.

C1.justification: The seven research questions and the abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about power effects, controllability, conversation progression and model differences. Changing 'linguistic coordination' to 'language coordination' is terminological.

C2.justification: New Appendix A adds literature-based cautions about unrealistic information access, excessive cooperation and missing human variation in social simulations, and broadens the discussion of role-play safety risks. Section 2 replaces specific workplace/online obedience claims with a general classic-obedience account. The original results interpretations and Limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Prompts, persona-processing instructions, decoding settings, hardware and timing disclosures, toolkit information and resource links are retained. Moving implementation details from Appendix E to F does not add reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds a substantial four-part Related Work appendix covering persona-based simulation, socio-cognitive biases, power-sensitive communication and role-play safety, with numerous new sources. It explicitly distinguishes the study from Tan and Lee (2025) and Wu et al. (2025), substantially expanding v1's dispersed research positioning.

P1.justification: Related Work becomes Appendix A, existing appendices are renumbered and cross-references are updated. Other edits concern terminology, the harmful-compliance background paragraph and the funding acknowledgment. The existing main narrative and experimental exposition are largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–24 retain their content and design. Local reflow changes spacing and page breaks: v1 keeps the 'Pronoun effect' heading with its prompt on page 12, whereas v3 leaves the heading on page 13 and the prompt box on page 14.

improvement.justification: The new Related Work appendix makes the contribution easier to assess against close prior work, particularly Tan and Lee (2025), and supplies useful cautions about interpreting social simulations. These benefits outweigh small editorial regressions: v3 introduces an unresolved citation in Section 2, duplicates the Echterhoff 2024 reference and separates a prompt heading from its box. The overall gain is limited to positioning and contextual explanation; the empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
